summary.intent: Execute all 4 plans in Phase 59 (FUSE IPNS Verify/Publish Hardening and Cleanup) using the GSD wave-based orchestration workflow on the cipher-box Rust FUSE crate.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 (59-01) completed successfully after rescuing from a mid-run 522 error — 95 tests passing, both findings (A+B) landed with proper TDD RED→GREEN commits. Wave 2 (59-02) was spawned sequentially but the transcript ends before its result. Waves 3–4 are still pending.

repo: Phase 59 has 4 plans in a strict sequential dependency chain (59-01→02→03→04), one per wave — there is no parallelism to isolate, making worktrees counterproductive here.
Root `npm test` runs `pnpm --parallel -r run test` (full monorepo) — too expensive for a Rust-only phase; scoped post-merge gate should be `cargo test -p cipherbox-fuse` instead.
winfsp build is CI-only on macOS — local winfsp/crypto-clippy compile failures are pre-existing and expected, not regressions.
The cleanup-wave tracking helper prints `commit_failed` as a false-negative even when the commit lands — known issue, do not retry.
config.json `_auto_chain_active` reset shows up as a dirty file between waves — benign, not a real change.

code.finding: Finding A (59-01): `build_folder_metadata` was swallowing `wrap_key` errors and publishing a `FilePointer` with `ipns_private_key_encrypted: None`, making the file permanently unrecoverable. Fixed to propagate the error.

Finding B (59-01): inode resolution used a cached CID/keys even when `file_meta_ipns_name` changed under an unchanged mtime, returning stale data. Fixed to force re-resolution on pointer identity change.

Finding C (59-02): `VerifyError::Legacy` was a unit variant; each match arm triggered a redundant second `resolve_ipns` call with a ~1ms race window against concurrent publishes. Migration to `Legacy { cid: String, sequence_number: String }` across 9 match-arm sites in 6 files eliminates the round-trip.

workflow: Worktree isolation is only beneficial when plans run in parallel; a sequential one-plan-per-wave chain should run directly on the phase branch to avoid merge/cleanup overhead and the #2070 SUMMARY-loss failure mode.

When a worktree genuinely needs node_modules, the subagent should run `pnpm i` inside the worktree — never symlink back to the parent checkout. The symlink approach bypasses husky/lint-staged correctness and leaves behind untracked files that cause cleanup-wave to fail.

The GSD #2070 failure mode: executor writes SUMMARY.md but the worktree is force-removed before it is committed, losing the summary permanently. Mitigation: rescue by committing the file before running cleanup-wave.
cleanup-wave helper fails closed on any untracked files in the worktree — must clear them before the merge step.

friction: Two Cloudflare 522 (connection timeout) errors hit mid-execution — one interrupted the Wave 1 subagent just before it could commit SUMMARY.md, requiring a manual rescue.
cleanup-wave helper had a mktemp template collision on first invocation, leaving the manifest variable empty and causing a no-op merge attempt.

Worktree approach was wrong for this sequential phase but was chosen by default (shouldDegrade=false) — caused unnecessary merge/cleanup complexity, the node_modules symlink hack, and the 522 near-miss on SUMMARY.
Subagent improvised a node_modules symlink back to the parent repo's copy so husky could find lint-staged — a symptom of using worktrees where they don't belong.
cleanup-wave blocked on the untracked node_modules symlink; required a manual removal step before merge could proceed.
open_items: Wave 2 (59-02): VerifyError::Legacy enum migration — spawned but result not yet returned in transcript.
Wave 3 (59-03): collapse dead `journal_entry` branch + `content_ops` dead bindings, remove dead field, fix test/vector.
Wave 4 (59-04): unify FUSE first-publish embedded sequence to `1`, remove `verify.rs` skew allowance.
winfsp and crypto-clippy build failures are documented pre-existing issues — not addressed in this phase.
GSD workflow default of enabling worktrees even for sequential phases could cause this same friction on future single-plan-per-wave phases.
